esc-living-traces-buccino-2026.about:
A forest is a living system made of relationships. Starting from this idea, a team of young international volunteers will spend Christmas in Buccino, a small village in inland Southern Italy, as a temporary transformative community. A different Christmas: not about shopping, but about people, nature and traditions, shared with a welcoming local community. Volunteers will plant agroforestry lines at the “Mimì & Peppino” Pedagogical Garden in Buccino, at the Cantiere Educativo in Postiglione and, with Hariba, within the Habitat Lab project in Oliveto Citra, preparing planting areas, mulching, composting, protecting young trees and creating habitats for biodiversity. At the heart of the experience is the presepe (nativity scene), which volunteers will build together with the local community. They will also join a day of traditional olive harvest.

Practical details: European Solidarity Corps team volunteering hosted by Associazione Costiera Amalfitana Riserva Biosfera in Buccino, Italy; activity period 5 weeks (30 November 2026 – 4 January 2027). Local transport to project activities, including the plantings in Postiglione and Oliveto Citra, is organised by the project team. Volunteers will receive non-formal and informal training through artistic workshops, practical activities, community work and experiential learning. The activity will be coordinated by Francesco Verderese and Mario Panzarella, who will guide the group throughout the project. As in every ESC project, volunteers get pre-departure and on-arrival training, a mentor, language support and a Youthpass certificate.

This program revolves around soil regeneration via permaculture and syntropic agroforestry techniques. We are reviving 30 hectares of degraded land to serve as a model for eco living and provide ways to ensure food and water security via regenerative practices such as Sytropic agriculture. The site is being transformed into a public park filled with biodiversity and a green playground for hosting our yearly music and art festival. You will be participating in various activities such as creating and maintaining agroforestry systems, organic gardening, developing the compost area and regenerative landscaping.

esc-culture-of-permaculture-prencov-2027.about:

Growing inside can be approached either in a philosophical, emotional, or mental way in our vision and understanding of the world. Growing outside can be related to gardening, relationships, nature, or our skills. Perma comes from permanent –something that can be sustainable. Culture is a complex of specific spiritual, material, intellectual and emotional traits of a society or social group, which also includes a common way of life, lifestyle, value system, traditions, and faith. We will explore together “What is perma-Culture?” not only in a material way, but also in philosophical, social, and also personal way.

It is a low-cost way for school and university students in western Georgia to try a real international competition close to home: strong local projects can be nominated for NASA's global judging, and the format teaches rapid prototyping, teamwork and pitching in a single weekend.

georgia-national-school-olympiad-2026-27.about:
The National School Olympiad (ეროვნული სასწავლო ოლიმპიადა) is the Georgian state's main academic competition for secondary-school students, administered by the National Assessment and Examinations Center (NAEC) under rules set by the Ministry of Education. Subjects are Georgian language and literature, Georgian as a second language (for non-Georgian-language schools), mathematics, history, geography, physics, chemistry, biology and foreign languages (English, German, French, Russian). Informatics runs in parallel through the separate GEOI olympiad.

It has three rounds. Round 1 is taken online from any computer during a set week in late November, with an optional practice test a few days before. Students who score at least 60% and rank in the top 1,000 in their subject go to round 2 (in January, at exam centres), and the best go on to the final round in March. In 2025-26 more than 19,600 students sat round 1, 7,800 reached round 2 and about 600 reached the final; 49 winners received diplomas and prizes from the Minister in October 2026, and winners could join the squads that represented Georgia at international olympiads.

The olympiad is free, recognised nationally and the standard first step towards Georgia's IMO, IPhO, IChO and IBO team selections, which the Rustaveli National Science Foundation runs in spring. Registration needs only the student's 11-digit Georgian personal number.
highlights: Official state olympiad in 9 subject areas, free of charge
Online first round from home, then rounds 2 and 3 at exam centres
Gateway to national-team selection for the international science olympiads
georgia-national-school-olympiad-2026-27.eligibility: Students at Georgian general-education schools (public or private) in grades 10-12 for each subject's age group; students at the basic level (lower grades) may also take part if they wish. Registration requires a Georgian personal ID number, so in practice it is open to students enrolled in Georgian schools.
how_to_apply: Watch naec.ge for the 2026-27 registration announcement (expected early November 2026)
Register online with your 11-digit personal number within the registration window
If you need special exam conditions, tick 'special conditions' and submit form N100 to NAEC or your regional education resource centre by the deadline
Take the optional online practice test, then sit round 1 online on your subject's day
If you qualify, print your invitation for round 2 and later the final round
georgia-national-school-olympiad-2026-27.costs: Free. Rounds 2 and 3 are held at NAEC exam centres around Georgia; travel there is at the student's cost.

geoi-georgian-informatics-olympiad-2027.about:
GEOI is the national olympiad in informatics (competitive programming) for Georgian school students, organised by the Association for Supporting IT Education and Informatics Olympiads on behalf of the Ministry of Education, with the Shota Rustaveli National Science Foundation handling team-selection invitations. Contestants write and debug C++ programs (as at the IOI), and solutions are graded by an automatic testing system on the association's contest server.

It runs in two stages across three age groups (grades 7-8, 9-10 and 11-12): a remote online first round, then an in-person final in Tbilisi (two contest days for grades 11-12). First-stage winners need at least 50% of the maximum; final winners need 60% and a top-ten place. The top ten in each age group who score at least one third of the maximum are invited to two selection rounds; the best four form Georgia's IOI team and the next four are reserves. The national team then trains in Tbilisi in June and at a camp in Bakuriani in July.

For any student in Georgia who enjoys algorithms, this is the most direct route to international competition, and the past problems with full solutions and tests on geoi.ge are excellent free training material.
highlights: Free national programming contest in C++ with an automatic judge
Three age groups from grade 7; online first round
Top 4 represent Georgia at the International Olympiad in Informatics
geoi-georgian-informatics-olympiad-2027.eligibility: Students in grades 7-12 at public or private schools in Georgia in the current school year. Contestants must be able to program in C++.
how_to_apply: Check geoi.ge from February 2027 for the registration notice
Register with the online form before the deadline (in 2026 it closed on 29 March)
Solve the online first-round problems on the contest system
If you qualify, attend the final in Tbilisi; top finishers are invited to the IOI team selection rounds
geoi-georgian-informatics-olympiad-2027.costs: Free. Finalists travel to Tbilisi at their own cost; national-team training is organised by the Ministry.

esc-international-scout-centre-rustavi-v.about:
The International Scout Center Rustavi (ISCR) is a non-political, non-profit youth movement in Rustavi, Georgia's third-largest city about 25 km from Tbilisi. It runs a scout centre and social enterprise that gives children and teenagers a friendly space for non-formal education, outdoor activities, citizenship and sport.

Volunteers join this European Solidarity Corps project for at least four months, with entirely flexible start dates until the end of May 2027. They help design and run youth activities and support the centre's social enterprise. Five volunteers share a renovated flat 5-10 minutes from the town centre, each with their own room, and receive money for food. The Dutch coordinating organisation Eastpackers runs an intake meeting and preparation day in the Netherlands (travel to it paid) and helps with the motivation letter and CV; in Georgia volunteers attend the National Agency's on-arrival and mid-term trainings and have a mentor.

This specific placement is only for legal residents of the Netherlands; volunteers from elsewhere should look for ESC projects in Georgia coordinated from their own country. It is a fully funded way to spend several months living in Georgia, learning youth-work methods and earning a Youthpass certificate.

Flexible start, minimum 4 months, until May 2027
Youth work with a scouting NGO near Tbilisi; Youthpass certificate
esc-international-scout-centre-rustavi-v.eligibility: Aged 18-30, legal resident of the Netherlands, available for at least four months, and no previous long-term (over 2 months) ESC volunteering. Must not be doing it to meet a study-programme obligation. Registration in the European Solidarity Corps portal is required.

Open the placement 'Youth Work in Georgia (flexible dates)' and apply with a motivation statement
Attend the intake meeting and preparation day with Eastpackers in the Netherlands
Agree your start date and complete pre-departure paperwork
esc-international-scout-centre-rustavi-v.costs: Covered by the European Solidarity Corps: travel, accommodation (shared flat), food allowance, pocket money and insurance. No fee.

eu-humanitarian-volunteer-tserovani-comm.about:
The Mtskheta-Mtianeti Regional Hub (MMRH) is a Georgian NGO based in the Tserovani settlement, a village built for people displaced from the South Ossetia region, about 30 minutes from Tbilisi. It works on peacebuilding, support for internally displaced persons and Ukrainian refugees, women's and youth empowerment and social enterprise.

The volunteer will strengthen the visibility and financial sustainability of organisations supporting displaced communities: designing a communication strategy, managing social media, creating content about the hub's work and the needs of IDP communities, running fundraising campaigns, developing newsletters and press materials, and reporting on performance. The deployment is nine months, starting around 1 December 2026, with an induction on arrival, capacity-building activities and field visits.

The volunteer lives in a house in Tserovani within walking distance of the office, with their own lockable room. Under the European Solidarity Corps humanitarian aid strand, travel, accommodation, insurance and a monthly allowance are covered. It suits graduates or students with communications, marketing or fundraising experience who want hands-on humanitarian work in the South Caucasus.

ibsu-un-model-peace-negotiation-simulati.about:
International Black Sea University (IBSU), a private university on the edge of Tbilisi, runs a series of free trainings for secondary-school students. Its 'UN Model: Peace Negotiation Simulation' is a fully funded project in which participants each represent a state or another actor and negotiate in an international-crisis scenario, aiming for a peaceful settlement and a joint agreement.

The format is a two-day intensive simulation for a limited group of pupils in grades 10, 11 and 12. It is designed to build critical thinking, negotiation and leadership skills in an international setting, and every participant receives a certificate from the university. Sessions are run in Georgian by IBSU's international relations and law faculty.

It is a good first taste of Model UN for students who have not yet been to a full conference, and adds a university-issued certificate to a CV or university application.

arab-reading-challenge-2026-2027.about:
The Arab Reading Challenge was launched by Sheikh Mohammed bin Rashid Al Maktoum to build a reading habit in Arabic among school students. Over one school year each participant reads books outside the curriculum and writes a one-page summary of each in a series of coloured 'passports' (red, green, blue, silver and gold, ten books each), reaching 50 books by the end. The 10th cycle (2025-26) drew more than 40 million students from about 60 countries, and national champions were crowned in Kuwait, Bahrain, Oman and the other Arab states before the Dubai final in October 2026.

It is open to students from grade 1 to grade 12 in public and private schools. Students register through their school and a supervising teacher, who submits the passports. Schools then run internal selection, followed by district and national qualifiers organised with each ministry of education, where shortlisted readers are interviewed by judges on their books, comprehension and expression. National winners travel to Dubai for the final. Arab students living outside the Arab world, and students of determination, compete in their own categories.

Prizes include AED 500,000 for the overall champion, AED 1,000,000 shared in the Distinguished School award, AED 300,000 for distinguished supervisors and AED 100,000 for the community (diaspora) champion. Beyond the prizes, it is an easy, free way to build reading, writing and public-speaking skills in Arabic, and a national title is a strong line on any university application in the region.

Read and summarise up to 50 books across five 'passports' during the school year
AED 500,000 champion prize and a final in Dubai
arab-reading-challenge-2026-2027.eligibility: School students from grade 1 to grade 12 who read in Arabic, in public or private schools in any participating country (including Kuwait, Bahrain and Oman). Arab students living in non-Arab countries can enter the community (jaliyat) track. Participation is through a registered school and supervisor.
how_to_apply: Ask your school's Arabic department or librarian whether it is registered for the 2026-27 cycle
Register through your school and supervising teacher (schools sign up on the official website)
Collect your reading passports and summarise each book you read on one visa page
Complete as many passports as you can (50 books for all five) and hand them to your supervisor
Prepare for the school, district and national qualifying interviews in spring 2027
arab-reading-challenge-2026-2027.costs: Free. No entry fee; schools receive the passports. Travel to the Dubai final for national winners is arranged by the organisers.

injaz-bahrain-company-program-2026-2027.about:
The JA Company Program is INJAZ Bahrain's flagship entrepreneurship programme. With the guidance of volunteer consultants from local companies, high-school and university students start, organise and operate an actual enterprise: they elect a management team, raise share capital, design and produce a product or service, market and sell it, keep accounts and finally liquidate the company and report to shareholders. Sessions run weekly during the school year and are supported by online learning material.

INJAZ Bahrain was founded in 2005 as part of JA Worldwide (INJAZ Al-Arab in the Arab region) and works with the Ministry of Education and universities across the Kingdom. The 2026 cycle ended with the 18th Young Entrepreneurs Competition, in which more than 1,100 students took part; winning school and university companies go on to represent Bahrain at the INJAZ Al-Arab regional competition.

The programme builds teamwork, leadership, negotiation, accounting and public-presentation skills, and it gives students a real business record and contacts with mentors from banks and companies. It is a strong extracurricular for anyone thinking about business, economics or engineering.
highlights: Run a real student company for a full school year
Mentored by volunteers from Bahraini companies
Winners go to the national Young Entrepreneurs Competition and the INJAZ Al-Arab regional final
injaz-bahrain-company-program-2026-2027.eligibility: Secondary-school and university students in Bahrain whose school or university partners with INJAZ Bahrain. Students can also register interest individually through INJAZ Bahrain's student inquiry form.
how_to_apply: Ask your school's careers or activities coordinator whether it runs the INJAZ Company Program this year
Or submit the student inquiry form on the INJAZ Bahrain website
Form a team and join the weekly sessions with your volunteer consultant
Launch, run and report on your company
Compete in the Young Entrepreneurs Competition in spring
injaz-bahrain-company-program-2026-2027.costs: Free for students; programmes are funded by INJAZ Bahrain's corporate partners.

reboot01-coding-institute-bahrain.about:
Reboot01 is an on-campus coding institute in Seef, Bahrain, built on the 01 Edu model (the same peer-to-peer, gamified method as 01 schools worldwide). There are no lectures: students learn by completing projects and 'quests' in teams, with the curriculum updated to current technologies. Graduates leave as full-stack developers, and the institute says they typically join companies at mid to senior level.

Admission has three stages. First you create an account and take a 90-minute online game test (memory and logic puzzles) that you can retake. Shortlisted candidates are invited to a full-time, four-week 'Selection Pool' in which they learn real coding material, sit weekly practical tests and do team assignments. Those who pass join the two-year professional programme; selection pools open several times a year, so there is no fixed semester.

No degree or coding background is required, only motivation and the ability to commit to two years. Training is supported by Tamkeen for Bahraini students, and payment plans are available for others. There is also a shorter AI Generalist workshop. It is a serious alternative or complement to a university computer-science degree for school leavers in the Gulf.

Project-based peer learning on the 01 Edu model
Rolling admission through an online game test
reboot01-coding-institute-bahrain.eligibility: Anyone aged 18 or over who has completed high school. No coding experience needed. Tamkeen funding applies to Bahraini nationals; non-Bahrainis can join with a payment plan. The programme is on campus in Bahrain.

Take the 90-minute online game test on a laptop (memory and logic games; retakes allowed)
If shortlisted, attend the four-week full-time Selection Pool
Pass the weekly practical tests and team assignments
Join the next two-year cohort
